NetScope 1.1: debug symbols, cross-references, security rules with SARIF, an obfuscation detector, version diff and new ways to install.

## Install

| | |
|---|---|
| Single-file binaries | `netscope-win-x64`, `netscope-win-arm64`, `netscope-linux-x64`, `netscope-linux-arm64` (self-contained) |
| dotnet tool | `NetScope.Tool.1.1.0.nupkg` from this release: `dotnet tool install -g NetScope.Tool --add-source <folder with the .nupkg> --version 1.1.0` (needs the .NET 8 runtime or later) |

Publishing to nuget.org and a Scoop bucket is prepared in CI and will be enabled in a later release.

All four binaries are tested and smoke-tested in CI on their own architecture. Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Each file has a build provenance attestation: `gh attestation verify <file> -R rorythebreaker/netscope`.

## New

- **PDB:** Portable PDB (embedded, next to the assembly or in `--pdb-path`, accepted only with a matching ID). It adds source lines to IL and CFG blocks, real local variable names to IL and pseudocode, and `source.file`/`source.line` to JSON. `--source` prints the source text.
- **Cross-references:** `--uses`, `--find-string` (`--regex`), `--field-refs`, `--fields`, `--strings`.
- **Security rules:** `--audit` with NS001–NS010 (process start, dynamic loading, reflection by name, unsafe deserialization, weak crypto, disabled TLS validation, hard-coded secrets, sensitive P/Invoke, SQL concatenation, registry and persistence). Also `--rules`, `--min-level`, `--fail-on` (exit code 4), `SuppressMessage` and `netscope.suppress`.
- **SARIF 2.1.0:** `--format sarif`, validated against the schema, ready for GitHub Code Scanning.
- **Obfuscation detector:** `--detect-obfuscation` gives a verdict (no, possible, yes), lists the signs and names the obfuscator.
- **Diff:** `netscope diff <old> <new>` for files or directories. Methods are matched by name and signature; you get IL and pseudocode diffs, call and complexity changes, metadata changes, new audit findings and `--exit-code`.

## Fixes

- JIT listings are bound to the method token, so overloads no longer mix up.
- Decompilations that time out are capped (`--max-abandoned`).
- The `--allow-run` helper runs in a sandbox: a Job Object on Windows, and rlimits, `prctl` and seccomp on Linux, with a memory limit (`--run-memory`), no child processes, and the helper dies when NetScope exits.
- Compiler warnings fail the build.
